one_line_contribution: A crossover estimand for agentic memory: at one fixed GEPA-optimized instruction, on the same test instances, compare the gain from the bank distilled from the episodes that instruction was optimized on ('own', cells 6 and 10) against the bank from episodes it never saw ('other', cells 7 and 9), so that the well-documented shrinkage of memory's gain at a better prompt can be split into headroom (any better prompt leaves less room) versus genuine information-specific absorption by the instruction container (S_info). The crossover is the new thing; the substitution framing and the compile-once prediction are not.
closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202), which the proposal itself concedes: Memento, ReasoningBank and GEPA on a shared 528/267 trajectory split, three backbones, four domains. It threatens the framing (the 'nobody has put a retriever and an optimizer on the same trajectories' sentence is already withdrawn) but not the estimand, because a side-by-side table cannot separate headroom from absorption without the own/other contrast. The residual novelty therefore rests entirely on an absence claim about EvoAgentBench's contents that the proposal admits it could not verify (PDF unopened, arXiv unreachable). Second: MIPROv2 (arXiv 2406.11695), whose instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint ablation on one training set is the two-container question for static demonstrations; it does not hold episodes out across containers, which is exactly the crossover's contribution, but a reviewer will compress Delta_info to 'the MIPROv2 ablation plus a train/train split with retrieval', and that compression is not unfair. Third: Experience Distillation (arXiv 2607.21051) already owns the retention-ratio shape with weights as the second container; swapping weights for an instruction is a cheaper and more deployable container but not a conceptually new measurement.
strongest_objection: The primary success criterion is a ratio the design is not powered for, and the quantity it IS powered for is not the quantity the title claims. Note that Delta_info algebraically reduces to acc(I1a x M_b) - acc(I1a x M_a): the acc(I x M0) term cancels, so the well-powered contrast (SE ~0.7pt, MDE ~2pt) is a bare provenance comparison between two banks at one instruction, which by itself licenses only 'a bank whose episodes the optimizer saw helps less than one it did not' - not 'most of memory's gain is substitutable'. The substitution claim lives in S_info = 1 - own/other, whose denominator reintroduces the M0 cells (5 and 8) and their noise. Run the proposal's own central scenario: G1 clears at g(I0,B_a) = 7pt, S_raw ~0.7 so own = g(I1a,B_a) ~ 2pt, headroom share at the predicted midpoint of 50% so other = g(I1a,B_b) ~ 4.5pt. Then Delta_info = 2.5pt, already below the pre-registered 3pt claim threshold, and S_info = 0.56 with SE ~0.20 by the delta method using the proposal's own SE(Delta_info)=0.7pt and SE(other)~1.0pt, giving a 90% CI of roughly [0.23, 0.89] - knife-edge against the required exclusion of 0.2, and failing outright if the gate clears at 6pt instead of 7, or if the headroom share lands at 60% instead of 50%, both of which are inside the proposal's own predicted 30-70% band. Prediction 1 thus fails under the proposal's median expected parameters, and the pre-registered fallback ('if mean(other) < 3pt, S_info is undefined') makes an uninterpretable primary the modal outcome. The Measurement section computes an MDE for Delta_info and for S_raw but never for S_info, which is the binding criterion. A second, cheaper failure mode compounds it: prediction 1 also demands direction consistency in both crossover directions, but G6 tolerates a 3pt bank-quality imbalance measured on S_dev n=300, where the SE of that imbalance estimate is ~3.4pt - the gate has essentially no power. A constant 2pt quality gap between B_a and B_b cancels in the two-direction mean (which is why the crossover is run both ways) but splits a true 2.5pt effect into ~0.5pt and ~4.5pt, so the both-directions requirement fails while the estimand is fine. Secondarily, and more likely to be voiced out loud in review: this audits the ExpeL/ReasoningBank evaluation template in a regime those papers never claimed, on 27-32B open-weight agents where the program's own prior study found the ExpeL bank TOST-equivalent to no memory (+0.6pt), after screening four agent x format pairings to find one where memory does anything at all, with the only larger-scale cell (gpt-oss-120b, cell 25) pre-declared 'never load-bearing' and Risk 11 refusing to reproduce any target's own setting.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Fix the estimand/power mismatch before freezing: either pre-register Delta_info as the sole confirmatory endpoint with S_info demoted to descriptive-with-CI, or power the ratio explicitly - report the analytic SE(S_info) as a function of the observed 'other' gain, and pre-register a gain-conditional threshold instead of a flat 'CI excludes 0.2'. If the ratio is demoted, cells 5 and 8 (8,000 episodes) stop being load-bearing for the primary and that budget can go into more optimizer seeds on cells 6/7/9/10, which is where the SE actually lives. 2) Replace the both-directions consistency requirement with a fitted direction x half interaction term, and measure bank balance on S_test n=1000 rather than a 3pt tolerance at S_dev n=300 where the SE of the imbalance is larger than the tolerance. 3) Add the full-data arms (see missing_baseline) so the paper says something about a system a practitioner could build. 4) Add a re-distilled B_a: same half-a episodes, different distiller model or an enforced paraphrase, so surface/textual redundancy with I1a is broken while episode provenance is held. Without it, 'own helps less' is equally explained by token redundancy between an instruction and a bank written from the same episodes by the same frontier distiller, which is not information absorption in the sense the title asserts. 5) Add a procedural positive control alongside B_a+dup10. Near-duplicate test questions with the same answers are non-substitutable by construction - no instruction can compress 100 specific answers - so prediction 6 is close to guaranteed and certifies only that the logging and pairing work, not that the instrument can distinguish absorbed from unabsorbed *procedural* value, which is the only kind at issue. A control that injects a genuinely procedural, instance-specific rule (e.g. a per-entity disambiguation step) would test the thing that matters. 6) Open the EvoAgentBench PDF before the design freeze rather than after; the entire novelty delta is an absence claim about its tables.
missing_baseline: The full-training-set head-to-head: I1_{a+b} x M0, I0 x M_{a+b}, and I1_{a+b} x M_{a+b} on all 800 training episodes. Every number in the grid - S_raw, S_info, the compile recommendation - is computed at 400 episodes per container because the halving is an identification device, and cell 18's 'recommended deployment' (I1b x C_a) pairs an instruction optimized on half b with a block compiled from half a, a configuration no practitioner would ever build. A reviewer will ask the obvious operational question - given my whole training set, should I optimize the prompt, build the bank, or both - and the plan as written cannot answer it, while the title and abstract clearly imply it can. Secondary omission: no bank distilled from half a by a different distiller (the re-distillation control above), so episode provenance and textual redundancy with I1a are never separated.
preprint_collision: The check is well above the usual standard for a proposal: a dated scan (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), 15 enumerated queries, 54 by-id verifications, committed scan records, a stated two-channel drop rule, and an explicit correction retracting v2's false negatives on five IDs. Credit for treating a failed search as a search failure rather than as evidence of absence. Two things nevertheless make it a weakness rather than a neutral. First, the check cannot support the claim it is being asked to support. arXiv is unreachable from the node and EvoAgentBench's PDF (2607.05202) was never opened, so the entire novelty delta - 'no combined optimizer-plus-memory cell, no token matching, no compiled-bank arm, no paired statistics' - rests on an abstract, a project page method list, and search-surfaced descriptions of Table 3. Combined cells and token-matched ablations are precisely the things that live in appendices and never appear in abstracts, so the search method is structurally blind to the one collision that would matter. The proposal's own stated residual risk ('a GEPA + memory ablation may exist in an appendix of a systems paper') names exactly the failure its procedure cannot detect. Second, the check already concedes that several non-primary claims are pre-empted in direction: compile-beats-or-matches-retrieve by arXiv 2608.14036 (skills > Workflow Memory by 6.06pt) and 2606.30775 (single rewrite ~ iterative refinement), which makes prediction 4 and secondary endpoint (a) confirmatory rather than novel, and Experience Distillation (2607.21051) already publishes the retention-ratio shape. I can independently verify only the pre-2026 anchors (ExpeL 2308.10144, ReasoningBank 2509.25140, Memp 2508.06433, A-MEM 2502.12110, GEPA 2507.19457, MIPROv2 2406.11695); every 2026 ID here is beyond what I can check, so the absence claims must be taken on trust from a channel the author has already flagged as insufficient. Verdict: no collision I can name kills the crossover estimand, but the proposal has not established that one does not exist, and it says so itself.
